The private-label brand, acting as a distributor of a body wash manufactured by a contract manufacturer, is required to file the Cosmetic Product Ingredient Statement (Form FDA 2512) if they are the distributor of the finished cosmetic product. According to 21 CFR 700.3(b), a "cosmetic product" means a finished cosmetic whose manufacture has been completed. The requirement in 21 CFR 720.1 applies to any manufacturer, packer, or distributor of a cosmetic product, regardless of whether the product enters interstate commerce. Therefore, as the distributor of the body wash, the private-label brand is responsible for filing Form FDA 2512 [1].

21 CFR 700.3(b) defines "cosmetic product" as a finished cosmetic whose manufacture has been completed; this definition confirms that the body wash, having undergone completion of its manufacturing process, qualifies as a cosmetic product under the regulation [2].  

21 CFR  720.1 requires either the manufacturer, packer, or distributor to file Form FDA 2512 for any finished cosmetic product, including those exported for sale in the United States [1].
